newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-LIU WINS WOMEN'S 200 BUTTERFLY WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-LIU WINS WOMEN'S 200 BUTTERFLY WORLD TITLE.

text.p: China's Liu Limin produced a storming finishing surge to win the women's 200 metres butterfly gold at the world short-course swimming championships on Thursday.

Liu claimed her third butterfly gold in three world short-course championships, coming through on the outside lane one to snatch a title which appeared to have turned into a duel between American Misty Hyman and Japan's Hitomi Kashima.
Hyman treated the crowd to her submarine skills, swimming the first length of the 25-metre pool under water and on her side until the last obligatory arm stroke above the surface.
Hyman, the fastest heat qualifier, took them through the first 100 metres inside world record schedule but by the 150-metre mark Kashima had overtaken her.

The odds looked firmly on Kashima but Olympic silver medallist Liu charged through on the eighth and final length to regain the title she won at the inaugural world short-course championships in Palma de Mallorca.
Liu, who won the 100 butterfly gold and 200 silver at the 1995 edition of the meet in Rio de Janeiro, clocked two minutes 7.20 seconds for the gold.
Kashima took the silver in 2:07.34 and Hyman the bronze in 2:07.54, ahead of China's Qu Yun in 2:08.74.
